          Plugin Studio becomes the place where everything SATOM automates lives: every plugin is an app (a flow or a script), apps get a page and result designer, SATOM steps (DDI, capacity, certificates, FortiWeb server policy), diagram analysis, actions and signed packages; code plugins and Report Studio packages move between servers without an update package. Plugin Studio is on the first level of the sidebar, Automation sits right above Plugins, and this release carries the fixes of the 2026-10-23 security review (certifi CA bundle, Wiki mail links, metrics range).

          Added

          • Plugin packages (.satomplugin, format satom.plugin/1): Report Studio can export a view or widget and import a package from another server, without an update package. Every file is checked against the manifest's sha256 and a signature must be trusted and valid; signed imports land in testing, unsigned in draft, a known slug updates in place (no silent downgrade, the publish gate re-runs for a published view).
          • Code plugins: a signed package can carry a Flask blueprint, installed under data/plugins/code/ and mounted at /x/<slug>/ behind sign-in at the next satom execute restart-all. Unsigned code is refused; every start re-verifies the signature and every file on disk, and a failing plugin is skipped, never stopping the app. Report Studio lists them with their state, Enable/Disable and Remove. Database: plugins.pkg_version, plugins.pkg_signer (migration plgpkg01).

          • Plugins menu (operator request): Operations → Automation → Scripts is now Plugins, a submenu with All plugins (the page) and one entry per published plugin the user may run, by name — the same access rule as the page. In the Global ADOM the published apps are listed there too, so the sidebar has one Plugins toggle.

          • SATOM steps in Plugin Studio apps (operator request, FA-0007): Render names, DDI: reserve an address / reserve by rules / release, Pick a FortiWeb by capacity, Certificate (issue or reuse), FortiWeb: create the server policy / remove a created policy. An existing DDI record is reused and never deleted; the record read back decides an allocation; a step that fails half-way undoes its own writes; only what a run created is undone on an error arrow; device writes need config_write; a rehearsal returns values of the real shape.

          • Diagram analysis and run overlay: Analyze explains every step (what it saves and reads, where its error goes, which undo steps that path reaches) and warns about unreachable steps, unsaved variables and a write without an error arrow after another write; Last run colours the steps by how they ended. An armed app run that writes is also a job with one log line per step.
          • App packages: a Plugin Studio app exports and imports as a satom.plugin/1 package of kind app — its data stores, its HTTP connections without secrets and their API Catalog versions travel with it; an import never overwrites this server's rows, connections or secrets.
          • Session-login connections: user + password posted to a login path under the base URL, the session cookie reused, one new login on a 401 (the DDI API).
          • SATOM list form fields: FortiWebs, approved WPP templates, Certificate Manager certificates, certificate providers, classification and segments.

          • New FortiWeb server policy app, round 2 (operator request): the form can take typed addresses instead of a DDI reservation (DDI: reserve by rules mode given: the DDI is not called, nothing typed is an error), the VIP interface per FortiWeb role (a list of the fleet's interfaces; empty = the FortiWeb rule's), and an existing server pool (a list of the fleet's pools; bound, never written or removed, checked on the device before any write). New lists: FortiWeb server pools and interfaces (local cache).

          • Certificate providers (operator request): the person issuing picks the provider (seed: Class E, internal only; Class C); the certificate remembers it for its renewal and revocation. Database: managed_certificate.provider, studio_apps.pkg_version, studio_apps.pkg_signer (migration spoflow01).

          • App actions in Plugin Studio → Apps (operator request): Disable / Enable (out of every menu, no run starts — operator runs, event automations, Run another app, Run a script steps; a saved script schedule is skipped, not paused), Download data (zip: runs and a CSV per data store), Reset (deletes the app's data from the database: its runs and the rows of the data stores only it uses; shared stores are kept and listed) and Delete (the app, its runs and the stores only it uses; a script app takes its script, versions, saved runs and credentials). Database: studio_apps.kind, studio_apps.script_slug, studio_apps.enabled (migration appkind01).

          • App designer (operator request: apps with "more style", cards and colours, "a web designer"): Plugin Studio → app → Design lays out the app's page (where each form field, the Run button and the result go, among headings, Markdown text, cards, columns, tabs, banners, callouts, images and link buttons) and its result (the run status, each Output step where the author wants it, number tiles, the action buttons and the steps), with drag and drop, an outline, undo/redo and a live preview drawn by the server. Styles: any hex colour (background, gradient, text, border) and fixed presets for spacing, corners, shadow, border, text size, weight, alignment and width; an app theme recolours the app's own area only. Blocks are drawn with SATOM's classes and there is no author HTML or CSS: Markdown without raw HTML, hex colours and presets re-checked when drawn. Images (PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP sniffed from the bytes, no SVG, 512 KiB, 12 per app) are served nosniff with default-src 'none' to the app's users and travel in the app package. Publish freezes the design; a field placed twice or a block naming a missing field, Output step or image blocks it; hard to read colours only warn. An app without a design is unchanged. Run outputs now carry their step key. Database: studio_apps.design_json, studio_app_assets (migration appdesign01).
          • Templates: what Plugin Studio → Examples installs is a template — it can be edited, disabled, reset and downloaded, never deleted. The Examples Remove button and route are gone, and every delete (app, script, data store, connection) refuses a template with the reason.

          Changed

          • Every plugin is an app (operator request: "everything created should be an app, even if it is only a script"): New app asks for the type, Flow (form + diagram) or Script (Python code with a form, run in the sandbox). A script app is the entry of its script — code, form, versions and audience stay in the script editor and on disk for the sandbox runner, which never holds a database connection. The Scripts pane is gone; scripts are listed in Apps with their type, and existing scripts get their app the first time an author opens Plugin Studio. The Plugins menu and All plugins page list flow and script apps alike.
          • Plugin Studio on the first level of the sidebar (operator request): it left Administrator → Studio and is an entry of its own, just above Administrator, in every ADOM. The Studio section is gone; Report Studio and Lua Studio are in Plugins in the Global ADOM too.
          • Automation sits right above Plugins, its entries alphabetical (operator request): in a device ADOM the Automation sub-menu moved from below WAF to Operations, just above Plugins (below Template Library); in the Global ADOM Plugins is no longer a sub-menu inside Automation but the one right below it, with the same entries for the same users. The Automation entries (API, Automations, Certificate Manager, Change Requests, Device Provisioning, Migration Report, System Provisioning, Upgrade Flow…) are sorted from their rendered labels, so the order is alphabetical in every console language and a new entry lands in its place by itself — the rule the Administrator sections already follow.
          • Studios renamed (operator request): Python Studio is now Plugin Studio and says it accepts Python code only; the custom-view studio that had that name is now Report Studio. Labels only — URLs and permission keys are unchanged. The plugin-package and code-plugin strings of the Report Studio page are translated into German, Spanish, French and Italian.

          Fixed

          • Report Studio and Lua Studio links did not pin their ADOM: in the Plugins menu (device ADOMs and Global) they were the only sidebar links without _adom=, so a new tab opened them in whichever ADOM another tab chose last. They pin it now, like every other entry.

          • The port of a Plugin Studio server policy was only a name: FortiWeb: create the server policy always bound the predefined HTTPS (443) or the default HTTP service, so a policy asked for 8443 listened on 443. A port that is not the predefined one now gets a custom service (created, or reused when the device has it; removed by the rollback only when this run created it).

          Security

          • certifi 2026.10.19 (pinned in requirements.txt, was unpinned and 2026.6.17 on installed nodes): earlier bundles trust the `emSign ECC Root CA
          • G3`, under which eight intermediates with compromised keys were issued (PYSEC-2026-4320 / GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2). SATOM's trust store starts from that bundle, so every outbound TLS check trusted them.
          • Wiki e-mail links followed the request's Host header: the absolute link in a follower's notification (and the source line of an export) was built from whatever Host the author's request carried, so it could point other users at another server. It now uses the same rule as the password-reset link: the request's host only when it is one of the node's own names or in LINK_HOSTS, otherwise the node's FQDN (services/link_host.py).
          • /api/v1/metrics/query accepted start/end = nan or inf: NaN fails every comparison, so it slipped past the range check into the store. Both must now be finite unix seconds (400 otherwise).
          • Defence in depth: the script vault's wrapped read and the Gitea probe of the infrastructure health page only open http(s) URLs (urllib also opens file://).
